mandatoryClauses.name: Reason to believe arrest
mandatoryClauses.description: Grounds showing applicant has reason to believe they may be arrested

mandatoryClauses.name: FIR/Complaint Details
mandatoryClauses.description: FIR number or complaint details, police station, offences alleged

mandatoryClauses.name: False Implication / Malafide
mandatoryClauses.description: Allegation of false implication or malafide intention of complainant if applicable

mandatoryClauses.name: Undertakings
mandatoryClauses.description: Undertakings by the applicant for the future, if granted anticipatory bail: to make himself or herself available for interrogation by the police as and when required, not to make any inducement, threat or promise to any witness or other person acquainted with the facts of the case, not to leave India without the Court's permission, and to abide by the conditions imposed. Never a statement of fact.

mandatoryClauses.name: Earlier Bail Applications
mandatoryClauses.description: Every earlier application for anticipatory bail or bail in this matter, with the court, the date of the order and the result, or that it is pending; or the blank where the brief does not say.

mandatoryClauses.name: Advocate Details
mandatoryClauses.description: Name and enrollment number of advocate

prayerTemplate:
PRAYER

In the light of the facts and circumstances stated above, it is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to:

a) Direct that in the event of arrest of the applicant {applicant} in connection with {firDetails}, the applicant shall be released on bail;
b) Pass any other order(s) as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the interest of justice.

And for this act of kindness, the applicant shall ever pray.

sections.description: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest
Special powers of High Court or Court of Session regarding bail

promptInstructions: Draft an Anticipatory Bail Application under Section 482 BNSS, 2023.

Begin with the facts that give the applicant reason to believe that the applicant may be arrested (for example a complaint, an FIR, a notice or summons received, or a threat), only as the BRIEF gives them. Do not add a fact the BRIEF does not give; where the BRIEF does not say what the apprehension rests on, write [To be confirmed: the facts on which the applicant apprehends arrest].

Set out the grounds for anticipatory bail that the BRIEF gives, and no others. Do not assert a ground (for example no prima facie case, false implication, malafide intention of the complainant, no criminal antecedents, cooperation with the investigation, roots in the community) unless the BRIEF states it. State each ground as the BRIEF puts it: do not add a reason or a detail to it. A submission on the law or the facts is written as "It is submitted that ...", among the grounds, never among the facts.

Address the nature and gravity of the accusation, the applicant's role, and the likelihood of the applicant fleeing from justice, as reasoning on the facts in the brief. Do not name any judgment; where an authority would normally be cited, write [Authority — add if relied upon].
Reference Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) section numbers — NEVER use old IPC section numbers.

Give the undertakings as undertakings by the applicant for the future, never as facts and never as undertakings by the advocate: the applicant undertakes that, if granted anticipatory bail, the applicant will make himself or herself available for interrogation by the police as and when required, will not make any inducement, threat or promise to any witness or other person acquainted with the facts of the case, will not leave India without this Hon'ble Court's permission, and will abide by every condition this Hon'ble Court imposes.
Use formal, respectful legal language appropriate for Indian courts.

State every earlier application for anticipatory bail or bail in this matter that the BRIEF mentions: the court it was made to, the date of the order and the result, or that it is still pending, each as the BRIEF gives it. Use a blank for any of these the BRIEF does not give. Where the BRIEF mentions no earlier application, do not say that this is the first application or that none is pending; write [To be confirmed: whether any earlier application for anticipatory bail or bail was made in this matter, to which court, and with what result].
Do NOT generate the verification clause or advocate signature block — those are added programmatically.
